prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
SNP 2019 Manifesto – summary (ideological framing preserved)

Core case
- Put Scotland’s future in Scotland’s hands. Westminster is broken, Brexit chaos proves it, and Scotland’s clear Remain vote has been ignored. A vote for the SNP is a vote to escape Brexit and secure Scotland’s right to choose independence.
- The SNP will seek an agreed, legally unchallengeable independence referendum (via Section 30), with a mandate already won. As an independent European nation, Scotland would always get governments it votes for, protect the NHS, tailor tax, social security, migration and economic policy, and invest in priorities instead of Trident.

Brexit and Europe
- Back a UK-wide second EU referendum with Remain on the ballot; if the only alternative to no-deal, revoke Article 50. Whatever the UK’s status, SNP MPs will protect Scotland’s place in the Single Market/Customs Union and alignment with EU standards.
- Johnson’s deal does not “get Brexit done,” threatens jobs, standards and the NHS, and drags on for years. Scotland has the right to choose a better future in Europe.

Ending austerity and tackling inequality
- Demand an end to austerity and reversal of Westminster cuts to Scotland’s budget; invest in services, wellbeing and productivity.
- Scrap the two‑child cap and rape clause, halt Universal Credit and punitive sanctions, end the benefits freeze and uprate income‑replacement benefits at least by inflation.
- Protect the Triple Lock; oppose pension age rises; back WASPI justice; restore Pension Credit and free TV licences for over‑75s.

NHS and social security
- Call for UK to match Scottish per‑capita NHS spend and pass an NHS Protection Act to keep health services out of trade deals and profit‑driven exploitation.
- Embed dignity and respect in social security; support carers, parents (Best Start Grants, Scottish Child Payment) and care leavers; expand paid parental leave and protections from redundancy.

Economy, jobs and fair work
- Devolve employment and migration to tailor Scotland’s needs; end exploitative zero‑hours, lift the statutory living wage to at least the real Living Wage, close the gender pay gap, strengthen worker voice on boards.
- Invest via the Scottish National Investment Bank; boost infrastructure, broadband/5G and city-region deals; support manufacturing, renewables, tourism (including exploring a VAT cut), creative industries and SMEs (tackling late payment).
- Reform energy markets to cut bills for households and small firms.

Climate emergency
- Match Scotland’s world‑leading targets (75% emissions cut by 2030; net zero carbon by 2040; net zero all GHGs by 2045). Keep EU environmental standards.
- Green Energy Deal: restore support for onshore wind/solar, back floating offshore wind, tidal and CCS; reform punitive grid charges; oppose fracking; decarbonise rail by 2035; accelerate EVs and green home heating; create a Net Zero Fund from oil and gas receipts; ensure a Just Transition for workers and regions.

Safer, fairer society
- Devolve drug policy; pilot supervised consumption facilities to save lives.
- Defend democracy: replace first‑past‑the‑post with STV, abolish the Lords, votes at 16, extend franchise to EU citizens, create an independent debates commission.
- Protect rights: keep ECHR/HRA, incorporate UNCRC, combat racism and bigotry.

Migration and asylum
- Scrap the hostile environment, protect freedom of movement, and create a tailored Scottish migration system (e.g., Scottish Visa). End indefinite detention, expand family reunion, reopen the Dubs scheme, and give asylum seekers the right to work.

Rural, food, fishing
- Safeguard CAP‑replacement funding, PGIs, and fair treatment for farmers, crofters and processors; strengthen the Groceries Code Adjudicator.
- Secure Scottish control of Scottish fisheries; protect seafood exports and workforce.

Defence, veterans, and foreign policy
- Scrap Trident and redirect billions to public services; retain bases and invest in conventional capabilities; give service personnel a statutory representative body; use vacant MoD homes for homeless veterans.
- Keep 0.7% aid, create a Climate Justice Fund, back human rights defenders; pursue peaceful solutions (e.g., Israel/Palestine two‑state), and uphold international law (e.g., Chagos).
